# $title reference material

$domain

This skill holds no copy of the documents below. Each block runs a command that reads the repository, so what you see is the branch you work on, not a snapshot.

Each block is one plain `git grep` command. Its `:/` pathspec names the file from the top of the repository, so the block works from the repository root and from each subdirectory, and in a linked worktree it reads the files of that worktree. Claude Code runs a load-time block only when it can analyse the command, and a block with `$$(...)`, `;`, `if` or a pipe stops a subagent from starting. If a block returns an error, your session is not in the repository. If a block returns no output, its reference file can also be missing or renamed. Each path in this skill is relative to the repository root, and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` prints that root.

A document of at most 200 lines, counted when this skill was written, is printed in full. A longer document gives its heading index and the command that reads one section of it.
